prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1178; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in on a roadway in Houston, Texas. Do you understand that this conversation is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full address for the record.

A: I'd rather just give the street and city, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me in your own words what happened?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road heading toward the intersection. The car in the oncoming lane drifted over the center line and we ended up almost head-on. I braked as hard as I could, but the impact still happened. It wasn't very fast, maybe a slow crash, but it felt violent.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, and the airbags did not deploy.

Q: Did you hit your head or lose consciousness at any point?

A: No, I didn't black out. I did hit my chest on the wheel and my head snapped back.

Q: Have you noticed any injuries since the collision?

A: My neck is stiff and sore, especially when I turn to check my blind spot. My lower back aches when I sit for long periods. I went to an urgent care clinic that afternoon and they said it looked like a strain.

Q: Have you had any prior neck or back problems?

A: Nothing serious. I had some occasional soreness years ago but nothing that needed treatment.

Q: Are you currently receiving treatment?

A: Yes, I'm doing physical therapy twice a week and taking over-the-counter pain relievers.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Just that I'm trying to get back to normal and I hope this gets resolved quickly.

Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the statement.
